key_responsibilities: Architect, implement and maintain a verification system for complex firmware/software
Write clean, robust, testable, reusable code for embedded test systems
Develop and maintain automated engineering tools to debug, analyze and test embedded products
Define assignments, schedules and quality expectations with project leaders
Debug and close out system issues in product firmware, software and systems

strengths: Every language/platform minimum qual has real depth: embedded C on Cortex-M4 bare-metal (STM32 Temperature Monitor - direct GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1 register programming, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, deterministic 1 Hz) and Python across ML, GUI and pipeline work

Bench instrumentation is first-hand, not listed-only: Oscilloscopes, Logic Analyzers, Multimeters, Spectrum Analyzers in Tools, and the JD accepts 'oscilloscopes OR logic analyzers' for that minimum qual

Debug-and-close-out is the single best-backed responsibility: COFFIN resolved 11 named integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to 100% pick reliability over 10 trials; Robocon fixed PWM saturation at 45 degree diagonals and sensor jitter via encoder-odometry feedback

Low-pin-count buses are load-bearing in multiple builds, not keyword filler: low-level I2C driver written on STM32, interrupt-driven UART command path to the Object Tracking Turret, TCA9548A I2C mux for dual VL53L0X ToF sensors in COFFIN
RTOS is real at task-coordination level - FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory coordination on the Object Tracking Turret, backed by CMPE 663 RTOS coursework

Verification methodology exists in one place and is strong there: the QAT project built a pure-integer reference model, exported 100 golden test vectors and a 17,024-entry hex weight file, then proved fixed-point requantization matched the float reference on 99.996% of hidden values at identical accuracy - that is golden-vector firmware verification in all but name

Automated engineering tooling has precedent: PyQt + Matplotlib real-time data-acquisition and visualization GUI built for a live lab environment at BARC, and CARLA automated data-generation pipelines producing ~8,000 labelled frames with zero manual annotation
Clean, modular, reusable code is demonstrable: Frame Simulator decoupled data model, math, visuals and UI into separate modules with a mix-in pattern centralizing transform-apply and refresh logic
real_gaps: No Pytest and no formal test framework anywhere in the profile - no unit, regression or parametrized test suite, which is the preferred qual sitting closest to the job's core deliverable
No CI/CD pipeline experience - GitLab appears only as version control, systemd only as single-service deployment; Jenkins, GitHub Actions, build/test automation on commit are absent

Never architected or maintained a verification SYSTEM - testing in the profile is per-project and ad hoc (10-trial reliability runs, <2mm repeatability checks, golden vectors for one MLP), not a reusable framework other engineers run against many firmware builds
No instrument automation stack - no SCPI/VISA/PyVISA, no programmable power supply, DAQ or electronic load control, no HIL rig; Apple test systems are built on exactly this
No battery or power-electronics domain exposure - nothing on BMS, cell characterization, charge/discharge cycling, coulomb counting or power measurement, and this req sits inside Battery Engineering
No JTAG/SWD probe workflow named explicitly (OpenOCD, ST-Link, gdb-on-target, trace) even though the hardware he used implies SWD flashing
No test-result reporting or data-infrastructure work - no log parsing/dashboarding of automated test output, which the 'present results and recommendations' responsibility implies at scale
overstated_by_keywords: Test automation - counted HAVE, but the backing is manual trial runs and one golden-vector exercise, not an automated suite
CI/CD pipelines - counted ADJACENT off GitLab and systemd; neither is a pipeline
JTAG / SWD - matched through the hardware-debugging alias; the specific probe tooling is never named in the profile
understated_by_keywords: QAT golden-vector verification (pure-integer reference model, 100 test vectors, 99.996% bit-level agreement) is firmware verification work that no JD keyword string-matched
BARC PyQt data-acquisition GUI is precisely an 'automated engineering tool used to debug and analyze' hardware, scored as nothing
COFFIN's documented 11-failure root-cause-and-fix sequence directly evidences 'quickly debug and effectively close out system issues' and never matched a keyword
Robocon interrupt-driven quadrature decoding written as a 4-bit A/B transition state machine from first principles shows the low-level reasoning a firmware test engineer needs
screening_gaps: Zero test-framework experience (no Pytest, no suite he owns) in a role whose whole output is a verification system - the first thing a hiring manager for this req checks
No CI/CD pipeline work at all; 'setting up, integrating or maintaining' Jenkins pipelines is a preferred qual he cannot speak to
No battery, power or cell-characterization domain exposure for a Battery Engineering team, and no instrument-automation (SCPI/DAQ/power supply) layer that test rigs are built on
llm_analysis.reasoning: The firmware half of this role is genuinely his: bare-metal C on Cortex-M4, I2C/UART/SPI drivers, FreeRTOS, scopes and logic analyzers, and the best-evidenced debugging record in the profile. The verification half is the gap - he has verification instincts (golden vectors, reference models, reliability trials) but has never built a test framework, never used Pytest, and never touched CI, which is the exact axis a verification-engineer screener probes. Worth applying because the minimum quals are fully cleared and the gaps are all preferred quals, but the Pytest and CI story has to be built before an interview, not during one.
